messages:
maya: quick update — spun up an llm.int8 (bitsandbytes weight-only) run on llama-3-13b in staging. memory footprint down ~46%, host GPU mem comfortably under limit, throughput +1.9x at batch=8, p99 latency -18% vs fp16.
omar: sweet. which eval slice did you run? full eval or targeted slices?
maya: core eval suite + focused slices for math/code/summarization. eval-bot posted the summary (pasted below).
eval-bot: run 1795006789-llmint8-run: model=llama-3-13b,llm.int8 weight-only; config: load_in_8bit=True, llm_int8_threshold=6, keep_fp32_modules=["lm_head","embed_tokens"].
eval-bot: metrics (delta vs fp16 baseline): overall EM/accuracy -1.2%, math slice -3.8%, code generation -1.1%, summarization -0.4%, avg perplexity +2.7%.
carla: thanks. math drop looks expected for weight-only int8. got any concrete failure examples?
maya: yeah — simple longchain arithmetic and multi-step substitution degrade. example prompt where fp16 solves but int8 hallucinates intermediate: "Compute 27*43 then add 158" — int8 sometimes reports wrong multiplication.
carla: ok. does accuracy correlate with sequence length or numeric tokens?
omar: preliminary slice shows correlation with long numeric sequences and low-temp decoding. also code generation shows more variable indentation/whitespace but logical errors are rare.
timo: thoughts on deployment strategy? I'm leaning to traffic routing by intent classifier: cheap/intensive queries => INT8; high-risk queries => route to fp16. we can measure risk via a small sentinel classifier or simple rules (contains \"math\", \"calculate\", codeblock).
maya: agree. also saw that enabling keep_fp32_modules for attention_norm helped a bit. micro-tweaks: keep_fp32_modules=["lm_head","embed_tokens","norm"] reduced math drop by ~0.9% but cost +4% memory.
carla: can we do dynamic fallback instead of upfront routing? e.g., run INT8, if token-level logprob drops below threshold then retry on fp16.
omar: that adds tail latency for some queries but keeps cost savings. we can use an async retry pattern: return INT8 answer plus background re-run on fp16 for requests marked critical. client gets fast answer and we send corrected result later if mismatch.
maya: quick config snippet I used:
```
# loader pseudocode
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("llama-3-13b", load_in_8bit=True, device_map="auto")
# keep some modules in fp32
config = {"keep_fp32_modules": ["lm_head","embed_tokens","norm"]}
```

carla: any perf numbers on the keep_fp32 tweak?
maya: throughput down from 1.9x -> 1.7x vs fp16 baseline, memory +4% vs pure int8 but still ~40% below fp16. worthwhile trade for targeted slices.
timo: propose rollout plan: 1) canary 5% traffic INT8 with analyzer hooks 2) intent classifier rules + 0.5% sample fallback to fp16 for randomized calibration 3) set quality alert: if math slice accuracy drop >2% over 30m, auto-scale canary down.
devops-bot: created canary deployment: infra/canaries/llama3-int8-2026-03-20 id=cny-179500. routing rule stub at /routes/canary-179500.
carla: what about eval cadence? we should run lit-evals every 2 hours on rolling sample to detect regressions fast. also store example failures for triage.
maya: +1. I'll wire eval-bot to push failing cases to /ml/triage/llmint8.
eval-bot: scheduled continuous eval: interval=2h, slices=[math,code,summarization,qa], alert_if_delta>1.5% (sliding 30m).
omar: also consider model variants: AWQ/GPTQ for comparison next week. int8 weight-only seems promising for many prompts but we need to quantify the cost/quality frontier and pick policy per-route.
carla: last question — any signs of hallucination class change (not just numeric errors)?
maya: rare but saw more factual assertion flips in long-context QA. probably quantization noise accumulates on deep recurrences.
timo: action items: maya run 24h continuous canary + keep_fp32 variant, carla assemble failure corpus, omar prototype intent classifier, eval-bot enable 2h eval and alerts.
maya: on it. will post logs and a tiny sample notebook to the thread. :thumbsup:
